phase: Phase 1 — catalogue only. Not read by the health engine; the eleven hard-coded ITSM rules in health/rules.js are unchanged.

schema.note: Transcribed from the Schema sheet. `fields` are the articulation and tracking fields the sheet defines, each with its purpose and fill rule verbatim; `required` marks them all as required, because the sheet says every rule carries them. `columns` maps every ITSM-sheet column to its catalogue field; four columns exist on the ITSM sheet without a Schema definition and are marked schema_defined:false.
schema.title: SAOS Rule Articulation Schema
schema.preamble: Every rule carries all ten articulation fields before it is built. Confidence Basis and False Positive Guard determine accuracy: a rule with an asserted confidence number gets discredited on first challenge, and a rule with no false-positive guard floods the estate.

fields.purpose: Stable identifier referenced by findings, evidence and remediation plans.
fields.fill_rule: Never reuse or renumber. A retired rule keeps its ID.
Must match a defined scoring dimension.

fields.purpose: The finding title the user sees.
fields.fill_rule: State the defect, not the fix. No thresholds in the title.
Systemic > Critical > High > Moderate > Low. Systemic = the governance mechanism itself is broken.
Explain how the defect arises. Never restate the rule title.
What breaks, for whom, and when. If you cannot name a consequence, the rule does not belong in the catalogue.
Name real tables and fields. This is the field that survives cross-examination in the demo.
Pseudo-query form. Must be re-runnable by the customer in their own instance.

fields.purpose: What is configurable and the default.
fields.fill_rule: Every threshold is configurable. State the default and the unit.

fields.purpose: How the confidence number is computed.
fields.fill_rule: MUST be a formula or a stated structural certainty. An asserted percentage is an automatic reject.
Records, counts, timestamps. A finding with no drill-down does not ship.
Every rule has a wrong case. If you cannot name one, you have not tested it.
Lane 1 direct apply (reversible data). Lane 2 staged update set. Lane 3 guided human decision.
Which domain causes this, or which this causes. The input to root-cause clustering.
Not Started / In Progress / Built / Deferred.
Not Tested / Tested on PDI / Tested on Customer / Failed.

severity_bands.description: The governance mechanism that should prevent defects is itself broken. One finding explains thousands. Weight 100.
Causes operational blindness, silently corrupts data, or makes a dependent capability return a wrong answer. Weight 40.
Materially degrades trust or blocks a capability. The system does not lie, it cannot help. Weight 15.
Real defect, contained blast radius, bulk-fixable, no immediate operational consequence. Weight 5.
Hygiene and completeness. Matters in aggregate, not individually. Weight 1.

severity_modifiers.conditions: Supports a Business Critical service | production environment | traced cause of downstream findings in another domain | duration beyond 30 days | shared infrastructure (network core, auth, shared DB) | silent failure (reports success, wrong result) | recurred after prior remediation | defect rate in class exceeds materiality threshold (pattern, not exception) | involves an approval, authorisation or segregation-of-duties control

Non-production and correctly tagged | class not consumed by any process | approved exception on file | below materiality floor for the class | compensating control evidenced | already flagged for retirement

worked_examples.text: CMDB-105 "CI with no owner, manager or support group" is base High. On a dev server nothing references: de-escalate twice to Low. On a core router supporting three Business Critical services: escalate twice to Systemic. Same rule, same data, two correct answers.

ITOM-017 "Credential authentication failing" is base Critical. On a lab subnet for two days: de-escalate twice to Moderate. On a production range for 31 days, causing 380 stale CIs, 1,847 lost relationships and zero-impact calculation on three Business Critical services: escalate past Critical to Systemic. This is the answer to "your tool will flood us with criticals".

rules.rule: Priority matrix producing a single dominant priority (>70% in one band)
rules.what_it_means: The priority matrix produces one dominant priority band for the overwhelming majority of incidents.
rules.why_it_matters: Priority stops carrying information. If 80% of tickets are P3, triage reverts to whoever escalates loudest, and SLA targets apply to a single undifferentiated pool.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.priority, impact, urgency; priority lookup configuration
rules.detection_logic: Priority distribution over the window; flag where one band exceeds threshold share
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 70% in one band. Window default 90 days.
rules.evidence_to_show: Priority distribution overall and by group, the matrix configuration, and the impact/urgency distribution feeding it.
rules.false_positive_guard: An estate where the workload genuinely is homogeneous. Compare against the impact/urgency spread before asserting.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — matrix reconfiguration as update set
rules.cross_domain_link: Degrades every SLA and prioritisation metric downstream

rules.rule: Categorisation taxonomy with categories never used, or one category absorbing most volume
rules.what_it_means: The categorisation taxonomy contains categories that are never used, or one category absorbs most of the volume.
rules.why_it_matters: Categorisation is the input to trend analysis, Problem identification and knowledge targeting. A taxonomy where everything lands in 'Other' makes all three impossible.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.category and subcategory, sys_choice definitions
rules.detection_logic: Category usage distribution against the configured choice list; flag unused categories and any category above threshold share
rules.threshold_parameter: Unused = zero use in 180 days. Dominance threshold default 40%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Category distribution with the configured list, unused categories, and the dominant category's subcategory spread.
rules.false_positive_guard: Seasonal categories legitimately unused in the window.

rules.rule: No SLA definition attached to a priority band
rules.what_it_means: One or more priority bands have no SLA definition attached to them.
rules.why_it_matters: Incidents in that band have no target and no breach measurement. They are invisible in SLA reporting, so the reported compliance figure excludes them entirely.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definitions and their condition scope, incident priority bands in use
rules.detection_logic: Priority bands with incident volume but no matching SLA definition start condition
rules.threshold_parameter: Any band with non-zero volume and no SLA
rules.evidence_to_show: Priority bands, volume per band, SLA definition coverage, and the reported compliance figure with and without uncovered bands.
rules.false_positive_guard: Band deliberately excluded from SLA measurement with documented rationale.

rules.rule: Assignment rules absent, so routing is fully manual
rules.what_it_means: No assignment rules exist, so every incident is routed manually.
rules.why_it_matters: Routing accuracy depends entirely on the person triaging. Produces reassignment churn, inconsistent routing for identical issues, and a first-touch delay on every ticket.
rules.source_tables_fields: Assignment rule definitions, incident assignment_group population method
rules.detection_logic: Incident volume with no matching assignment rule at creation
rules.threshold_parameter: Report as a ratio of total volume
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio of manually routed incidents, the reassignment count distribution for them, and time-to-first-assignment.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate manual triage model with a staffed dispatch function.

rules.rule: Impact and urgency fields not driving priority (priority set manually, overriding matrix)
rules.what_it_means: Priority is being set manually rather than derived from impact and urgency, overriding the matrix.
rules.why_it_matters: The matrix exists and is bypassed. Priority becomes a judgement call, which means it is inconsistent between people and cannot be audited.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.priority, impact, urgency; sys_audit on priority field
rules.detection_logic: Incidents whose priority differs from the matrix result for their impact and urgency values
rules.threshold_parameter: Report as a ratio and by group
rules.evidence_to_show: Override ratio, distribution by group and user, the direction of override, and the matrix result versus the set value.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate override workflow with a documented justification field.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — enforce via data policy, or make override require a reason

rules.rule: Category-subcategory combinations invalid or orphaned
rules.what_it_means: Category and subcategory combinations in use are invalid or orphaned relative to the configured dependency.
rules.why_it_matters: Reporting groups on combinations that do not exist in the taxonomy. Trend analysis splits across phantom categories.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.category and subcategory, sys_choice dependency configuration
rules.detection_logic: Incident category/subcategory pairs not present in the configured dependent choice set
rules.threshold_parameter: Any invalid pair with non-zero volume
rules.evidence_to_show: Invalid pair list with volume, the valid dependency configuration, and the source writing them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Choice retired while historical records legitimately retain the old value. Scope to open and recent records.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 for the records, Lane 2 for the validation gap

rules.rule: Auto-close duration set so short that resolution verification is impossible
rules.what_it_means: Auto-close duration is set so short that the caller cannot realistically verify the resolution before closure.
rules.why_it_matters: Incidents close before anyone confirms the fix worked. Suppresses the reopen rate, which then reads as high quality when it is measurement failure.
rules.source_tables_fields: Auto-close configuration, resolution-to-close interval distribution, reopen rate
rules.detection_logic: Auto-close duration below threshold, correlated against reopen rate and reopen timing
rules.threshold_parameter: Default minimum 3 business days. Compare against the reopen timing distribution.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the configuration. The suppression effect is evidenced by reopen timing.
rules.evidence_to_show: Auto-close duration, reopen rate, reopen timing distribution showing reopens clustered just after the window.
rules.false_positive_guard: Short window appropriate for a specific category with genuine instant verification.

rules.rule: Resolution code list with a dominant catch-all value ("Other", "Resolved")
rules.what_it_means: The resolution code list has a catch-all value absorbing a dominant share of closures.
rules.why_it_matters: Resolution codes are the input to Problem identification and knowledge targeting. When most closures are 'Other', neither can function.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.close_code distribution, sys_choice list
rules.detection_logic: Resolution code distribution; flag where a catch-all or generic value exceeds threshold share
rules.evidence_to_show: Code distribution, the configured list, and the distribution by group to identify where the habit concentrates.
rules.false_positive_guard: A genuinely broad code used correctly for a narrow category.

rules.rule: State model with unreachable or dead-end states
rules.what_it_means: The incident state model contains states that cannot be reached, or states with no valid transition out.
rules.why_it_matters: Records get stuck in a dead-end state and drop out of every operational view. They are neither open nor closed in any report.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident state choices, state transition configuration, actual state distribution
rules.detection_logic: States with zero records (unreachable) or records in a state with no outbound transition and age above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 30 days for dead-end detection
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on transition configuration and record distribution.
rules.evidence_to_show: State list with record counts, transition map, and the records stuck in dead-end states with their ages.
rules.false_positive_guard: State reserved for a workflow not yet live.

rules.rule: Mandatory fields enforced at the wrong state (too late to be useful)
rules.what_it_means: Mandatory fields are enforced at a state so late in the lifecycle that the information is no longer useful.
rules.why_it_matters: Requiring a category at closure means categorisation is a closing formality rather than a triage input. The field is populated and the data is worthless.
rules.source_tables_fields: UI policy and data policy mandatory configuration by state, field population timing from audit
rules.detection_logic: Mandatory enforcement at closure states for fields whose operational value is at triage
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — the judgement about when a field is useful is encoded in configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Field, the state where it becomes mandatory, the population timing distribution from audit, and the operational use of that field.
rules.false_positive_guard: Field genuinely only knowable at closure.

rules.rule: Notification rules firing to inactive users or empty groups
rules.what_it_means: Notification rules resolve to inactive users or groups with no active members.
rules.why_it_matters: The notification fires and reaches nobody. The rule reports as executed, so no failure is recorded anywhere.
rules.source_tables_fields: Notification rule recipients, sys_user.active, sys_user_grmember
rules.detection_logic: Notification rules whose recipients resolve to inactive users or empty groups
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the recipient resolves to someone active or does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, recipient configuration, resolved recipient state, firing volume, and the incidents affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Recipient deactivated within a grace period with a delegate configured.

rules.rule: Business hours / schedule not applied to SLA calculation
rules.what_it_means: SLA calculation is running on calendar time where business hours were intended, or no schedule is attached.
rules.why_it_matters: Targets are effectively tighter or looser than committed. A four-hour business-hours commitment enforced as four calendar hours breaches every weekend.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definition schedule attachment, commitment definitions, breach distribution by day of week
rules.detection_logic: SLA definitions with no schedule, or whose schedule contradicts the commitment they enforce
rules.threshold_parameter: Compare against the service commitment where one exists
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration. The mismatch against commitment depends on commitment records existing.
rules.evidence_to_show: SLA definition, its schedule, the commitment it enforces, and the breach distribution by day of week and hour.
rules.false_positive_guard: 24x7 genuinely intended.
rules.cross_domain_link: Commercial consequence where SLAs back contracts

rules.rule: Custom incident states added without corresponding SLA handling
rules.what_it_means: Custom incident states have been added without corresponding SLA pause, resume or stop handling.
rules.why_it_matters: The SLA clock behaves unpredictably in the custom state. Usually it keeps running when it should pause, producing breaches that are configuration artefacts.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident state choices vs OOB set, SLA definition pause and stop conditions
rules.detection_logic: Custom states not referenced in any SLA pause or stop condition, with non-zero record volume
rules.threshold_parameter: Any custom state absent from SLA conditions
rules.evidence_to_show: Custom state, record volume, time spent in it, and the SLA conditions that do not account for it.
rules.false_positive_guard: State deliberately intended to accrue SLA time.

rules.rule: Incident form with excessive custom fields, unpopulated
rules.what_it_means: The incident form carries custom fields that are largely unpopulated.
rules.why_it_matters: Form clutter, slower triage, and upgrade surface for data nobody captures. Low consequence individually, cumulative across a form with thirty custom fields.
rules.source_tables_fields: Custom fields on incident, population rates
rules.detection_logic: Custom incident fields with population rate below threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Field list with population rate, creation date, and creating update set.
rules.false_positive_guard: Fields for a programme not yet live.

rules.rule: Knowledge suggestion not enabled on incident
rules.what_it_means: Knowledge suggestion is not enabled on the incident form.
rules.why_it_matters: Agents cannot see relevant articles at the point of need, so knowledge is written and never consumed. Undermines the entire Problem-to-Known-Error chain.
rules.source_tables_fields: Knowledge suggestion configuration on incident, knowledge article volume and view counts
rules.detection_logic: Knowledge suggestion disabled or unconfigured on incident where a knowledge base exists with published articles
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires only where published articles exist
rules.evidence_to_show: Configuration state, published article count, article view distribution, and the incident volume that could have matched.
rules.false_positive_guard: Knowledge surfaced through a different mechanism.
rules.cross_domain_link: Breaks the Known Error consumption chain

rules.rule: Percentage of incidents with no CI and no service reference
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of incidents referencing neither a CI nor a service.
rules.why_it_matters: These incidents cannot be aggregated by anything the CMDB knows about. Trend analysis, Problem identification and service-level reporting all exclude them silently.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.cmdb_ci, incident.business_service, incident volume
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(incidents with both fields empty) / COUNT(incidents) in the window
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio trend, distribution by category and group, and the categories where reference rates are highest for contrast.
rules.false_positive_guard: Categories where neither reference is meaningful: HR, facilities, access requests.
rules.cross_domain_link: The processes are operating without the CMDB

rules.rule: Percentage of incidents referencing a bare CI rather than a Business Service
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of incidents referencing a bare CI rather than a Business Service.
rules.why_it_matters: Service-level reporting is impossible. Incidents cannot be rolled up to the services the business recognises, so the service view is built from assumptions rather than data.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.cmdb_ci vs business_service population
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(incidents with cmdb_ci but no business_service) / COUNT(incidents with either)
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio by group and category, and whether the referenced CIs have a traversable path to a service.
rules.false_positive_guard: Service model deliberately not used for incident classification.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2; Lane 3 where the CSDM path is missing

rules.rule: Incident assigned to a group with zero active members
rules.what_it_means: Incidents are assigned to a group that has zero active members.
rules.why_it_matters: The ticket is in a queue nobody can see. It ages invisibly until someone escalates by another route. A populated assignment field that routes to nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.assignment_group, sys_user_grmember, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Open incidents whose assignment group resolves to zero active members
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — resolves to a person or does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Incident count by group, their ages, priorities, the empty groups, and their last membership change date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Group emptied within hours with a reassignment in progress.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — reassignment is an operational decision
rules.cross_domain_link: Cross-links to CMDB-102 and Data Quality Q2

rules.rule: Incident referencing a retired or non-existent CI
rules.what_it_means: Incidents reference a CI that is retired or no longer exists.
rules.why_it_matters: Work is tracked against infrastructure that officially does not exist. Impact calculations for the incident traverse from a dead record.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.cmdb_ci, cmdb_ci existence and lifecycle state
rules.detection_logic: Incidents referencing a CI sys_id with no record, or a CI in a retired state
rules.evidence_to_show: Incident list, the referenced CI and its state, and the live CI the incident probably concerns.
rules.false_positive_guard: Incident deliberately raised to complete a decommission.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the correct CI is unambiguous, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Resolution notes empty or below a meaningful length
rules.what_it_means: Resolution notes are empty or below a length that could carry meaning.
rules.why_it_matters: The resolution is not recorded. The next occurrence starts from nothing, knowledge cannot be written, and Problem analysis has no material to work with.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.close_notes, resolution fields, length distribution
rules.detection_logic: Resolved incidents with empty resolution notes or length below threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Length threshold default 20 characters after trimming
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by group and resolution code, length distribution, and the reopen rate for these incidents versus properly documented ones.
rules.false_positive_guard: Categories where resolution is self-evident from the close code.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — this is a behaviour change, not a data fix

rules.rule: Resolution notes containing only a copy of the short description
rules.what_it_means: Resolution notes contain only a copy of the short description.
rules.why_it_matters: Passes any length check while carrying zero information. The most common way a resolution-notes mandatory field is defeated.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.short_description and close_notes, similarity comparison
rules.detection_logic: Resolved incidents where close_notes similarity to short_description exceeds threshold
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — high similarity is strong evidence but a genuine restatement is possible.
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by group, sample pairs, and the distribution showing the habit concentrating in specific groups.
rules.false_positive_guard: Short incidents where the description genuinely is the resolution.

rules.rule: Caller field populated with a service account or generic user
rules.what_it_means: The caller field is populated with a service account or a generic shared user.
rules.why_it_matters: The real requester is unknown. Notifications go nowhere useful, satisfaction measurement is impossible, and the incident cannot be attributed to a department or location.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.caller_id, sys_user account type indicators
rules.detection_logic: Incidents whose caller resolves to a service account, integration user, or a user above a volume threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Volume threshold configurable; service account detection from naming and role pattern
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — service account classification is inferred from naming and role.
rules.evidence_to_show: Caller distribution, the generic callers with volume, and the incident sources that populate them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately automated incidents where no human caller exists.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — populate a real caller at the integration

rules.rule: Short description duplicated across large volumes (template pasting)
rules.what_it_means: The same short description text appears across a large volume of incidents.
rules.why_it_matters: Template pasting. Real symptom detail is lost, so clustering for Problem identification produces one giant meaningless cluster.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.short_description frequency distribution
rules.detection_logic: Short description values appearing above a volume threshold, normalised
rules.threshold_parameter: Volume threshold configurable relative to total volume
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on frequency. The interpretation as template pasting is inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Repeated descriptions with volume, the groups producing them, and the resolution code distribution for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely recurring identical incidents from an automated source, which is a Problem finding rather than a data one.

rules.rule: Category not matching the resolution code pattern for that category
rules.what_it_means: The category does not match the resolution code pattern typical for that category.
rules.why_it_matters: Either the categorisation or the closure is wrong. Detected as a mismatch, resolved by looking at which of the two the group gets right elsewhere.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.category and close_code, joint distribution
rules.detection_logic: Category and close code pairs occurring far outside the expected joint distribution
rules.threshold_parameter: Expected distribution derived from the estate's own data, minimum volume per category required
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — derived from the estate's own patterns, so it inherits their consistency.
rules.evidence_to_show: The mismatched pairs with volume, the expected joint distribution, and the groups producing them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately broad categories with diverse resolutions.
rules.cross_domain_link: Indicates either categorisation or closure error

rules.rule: Close code and close notes inconsistent
rules.what_it_means: The close code and close notes are inconsistent — the notes describe something the code does not match.
rules.why_it_matters: Reporting by close code is wrong for these records. Whichever of the two is used produces a different picture.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.close_code and close_notes, semantic consistency check
rules.detection_logic: Incidents whose close notes content contradicts the close code semantics
rules.threshold_parameter: Consistency rules per close code, derived from the estate's own dominant patterns
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — semantic consistency checking is the least certain rule in this group. Report with samples and let the customer validate.
rules.evidence_to_show: Sample records with both fields, the expected note pattern for the code, and the volume by group.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate edge cases. Requires human validation before bulk action.

rules.rule: Incident with no work notes at all through its lifecycle
rules.what_it_means: An incident passes through its entire lifecycle with no work notes recorded.
rules.why_it_matters: No audit trail of what was done. For a regulated entity this is an evidence gap, and for the next occurrence it means starting from zero.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident work notes journal entries, incident lifecycle
rules.detection_logic: Resolved incidents with zero work note entries
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report by group and priority
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by group and priority, the duration these incidents were open, and the reassignment count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Trivial incidents resolved at first contact.

rules.rule: Attachment-only resolution with no text record
rules.what_it_means: The resolution is recorded only as an attachment with no text record.
rules.why_it_matters: The resolution is not searchable, not analysable, and not usable for knowledge. It exists for one human who opens the file.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident close_notes population, sys_attachment on resolved incidents
rules.detection_logic: Resolved incidents with empty close notes but attachments added near resolution
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by group, the attachment types, and the empty text fields.
rules.false_positive_guard: Attachment supplementing adequate text notes.

rules.rule: Free-text fields containing PAN, Aadhaar, account numbers, or other identifiers (DPDP exposure)
rules.what_it_means: Free-text fields on incidents contain patterns matching PAN, Aadhaar, account numbers or other personal identifiers.
rules.why_it_matters: A DPDP exposure sitting in a table with broad read access. The incident process is the most common route for personal data to enter ServiceNow unclassified.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident description, short_description, work notes, close_notes; regex pattern set
rules.detection_logic: Free-text fields matching identifier patterns, counted by field and pattern type
rules.threshold_parameter: Pattern set per identifier type, with checksum validation where the format supports it
rules.confidence_basis: Pattern match with checksum validation at 95%; pattern alone at 75%. Always report the two separately.
rules.evidence_to_show: COUNT AND LOCATION ONLY — never the matched values. Report field, pattern type, count, and the ACL state on those fields.
rules.false_positive_guard: False pattern matches on unrelated numeric strings. Checksum validation where available removes most.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — redaction is a data protection decision, not a bulk edit
rules.cross_domain_link: Feeds DPDP Compliance Manager and the Regulatory Evidence Pack

rules.rule: Location or department unpopulated where routing depends on it
rules.what_it_means: Location or department is unpopulated on incidents where routing logic depends on those fields.
rules.why_it_matters: Routing falls back to a default queue. The incident reaches the wrong team first and the delay is attributed to triage rather than to data.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.location and department, assignment rules referencing them
rules.detection_logic: Incidents with empty location or department where an assignment rule evaluates those fields
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires only where routing rules reference the fields
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state and rule reference.
rules.evidence_to_show: Incident count, the routing rules that evaluate the empty field, and the reassignment rate for these incidents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Routing rules that handle the empty case correctly.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where inferable from the caller record, Lane 2 for the enforcement gap
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-020 and ITOM-004 location chain

rules.rule: Reopen rate above threshold, by group and by resolution code
rules.what_it_means: The reopen rate exceeds threshold, measured by group and by resolution code.
rules.why_it_matters: Reopens mean the fix did not work. Broken down by group and code, the rate points directly at where resolution quality is failing rather than at a general complaint.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident reopen events from audit, resolution codes, assignment groups
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(reopened incidents) / COUNT(resolved incidents), by group and by close code
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio. Reopen detection from state audit.
rules.evidence_to_show: Reopen rate overall, by group, by code, with the time-to-reopen distribution and resolution note quality for reopened incidents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Reopen used procedurally for related follow-up rather than for failure.

rules.rule: Auto-close used as the primary closure mechanism (resolution never verified)
rules.what_it_means: Auto-close is the primary closure mechanism, so resolutions are never verified by the caller.
rules.why_it_matters: Closure becomes a timer rather than a confirmation. The reopen rate is artificially suppressed and satisfaction data is absent.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident closure method distribution, auto-close job attribution
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(auto-closed incidents) / COUNT(closed incidents)
rules.evidence_to_show: Closure method distribution, auto-close duration, reopen timing, and the caller confirmation rate where captured.
rules.false_positive_guard: Categories where caller confirmation is genuinely not applicable.

rules.rule: Reassignment count distribution with a long tail (ticket ping-pong)
rules.what_it_means: The reassignment count distribution has a long tail — a significant population of incidents bouncing between groups.
rules.why_it_matters: Each reassignment adds delay and loses context. The tail is where customer experience is worst and where the routing model is failing.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident reassignment_count, assignment audit history
rules.detection_logic: Reassignment count distribution; flag the tail above threshold and the group pairs involved
rules.evidence_to_show: Distribution, the tail population with resolution times, and the group-pair transition matrix showing where tickets bounce.
rules.false_positive_guard: Complex incidents legitimately requiring multiple specialists.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3; Lane 2 where assignment rules can resolve the common paths
rules.cross_domain_link: Symptom of ITSM-004 and categorisation failure

rules.rule: SLA breach rate above threshold
rules.what_it_means: The SLA breach rate exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: The headline SLA measure. Only meaningful alongside the configuration findings, because a breach rate computed on misconfigured SLAs measures the configuration rather than the service.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla breach records, SLA definitions, incident volume
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(breached SLAs) / COUNT(SLAs attached), by definition and by group
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold from the customer's own commitment; default 10%
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio, conditional on SLA configuration being sound. Report ITSM-003 and ITSM-012 alongside.
rules.evidence_to_show: Breach rate by definition, group and priority, with breach timing distribution and the SLA configuration for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Breaches caused by SLA misconfiguration rather than service failure. Report the configuration findings first.
rules.cross_domain_link: Only valid once the SLA configuration findings are resolved

rules.rule: SLA paused or cancelled at abnormal rates (gaming)
rules.what_it_means: SLA records are being paused or cancelled at abnormal rates.
rules.why_it_matters: Pause and cancel stop the clock. Abnormal rates suggest the mechanism is being used to manage the metric rather than to reflect genuine waiting. A control integrity finding rather than a performance one.
rules.source_tables_fields: task_sla pause and cancel events, duration in paused state
rules.detection_logic: Pause and cancel rates by group and by definition, against the estate distribution; plus paused duration exceeding active duration
rules.threshold_parameter: Default flag at 2x the estate mean rate
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the rates. The gaming interpretation is inferred and should be stated as such.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pause and cancel rates by group, paused versus active duration, the pause reasons where captured, and the on-hold state correlation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate high-pause workload, such as incidents awaiting third-party vendors.
rules.cross_domain_link: Control integrity; route to audit as well as operations

rules.rule: Resolution time distribution with a spike immediately before SLA expiry
rules.what_it_means: The resolution time distribution shows a spike immediately before SLA expiry.
rules.why_it_matters: Work is being timed to the target rather than to the problem. Statistically unmistakable and difficult to explain any other way.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident resolution timestamps, task_sla target times, resolution-to-target interval distribution
rules.detection_logic: Resolution time distribution relative to SLA target; flag a spike in the final decile before expiry
rules.threshold_parameter: Spike threshold default 2x the expected density for that interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the distribution. The interpretation is strongly evidenced by the shape.
rules.evidence_to_show: Resolution timing histogram relative to target, by group and priority, with the expected distribution overlaid.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuine prioritisation pressure producing a natural clustering near targets.
rules.cross_domain_link: Control integrity; strong evidence of metric management

rules.rule: Incidents resolved and closed within seconds of creation (bulk closure)
rules.what_it_means: Incidents are resolved and closed within seconds of creation, in volume.
rules.why_it_matters: Bulk closure. Either an automated process is closing records without action, or someone is clearing a backlog by closing it.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident creation, resolution and closure timestamps, closing user
rules.detection_logic: Incidents whose create-to-close interval is below threshold, grouped by closing user and by time window
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by closing user and time window, the close codes used, resolution note state, and whether they clustered in bursts.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate automated resolution for self-healing conditions.
rules.cross_domain_link: Control integrity; distorts every volume and resolution metric

rules.rule: Backlog ageing beyond threshold by priority
rules.what_it_means: The incident backlog is ageing beyond threshold, by priority band.
rules.why_it_matters: Backlog age by priority is what tells you whether the queue is being worked or merely held. A growing P2 backlog with a healthy P1 backlog is a capacity signal.
rules.source_tables_fields: Open incident ages by priority
rules.detection_logic: Open incidents exceeding age threshold per priority band, with trend
rules.threshold_parameter: Age thresholds per priority; defaults 2 days P1, 5 days P2, 15 days P3
rules.evidence_to_show: Age distribution by priority and group, backlog trend, and the oldest records with their last activity date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Records legitimately parked awaiting a third party, correctly on hold.

rules.rule: P1 raised manually where automated conditions existed
rules.what_it_means: P1 incidents are being raised manually in situations where automated conditions existed and should have triggered.
rules.why_it_matters: The automation was configured and did not fire, so the detection depended on a human noticing. Detection time is the difference between a four-minute response and a seventeen-minute one.
rules.source_tables_fields: P1 incidents, their creation source, alert and event correlation in the preceding window
rules.detection_logic: Manually created P1 incidents with a correlated alert in the preceding window that did not auto-create
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — correlation between alert and incident is circumstantial without an explicit link.
rules.evidence_to_show: The incident, the correlated alert, the alert rule state, and the time between alert and manual creation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely human-detected issues with a coincidental alert.

rules.rule: P1 volume without corresponding Problem records
rules.what_it_means: P1 volume exists with no corresponding Problem records.
rules.why_it_matters: Major incidents are being resolved and never analysed. The same cause will produce the same P1 again, and each occurrence starts from nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: P1 incident volume, linked Problem records
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(P1 incidents with no linked Problem) / COUNT(P1 incidents)
rules.evidence_to_show: P1 list with Problem linkage state, their close codes, and the recurrence pattern among unanalysed P1s.
rules.false_positive_guard: P1s with a genuinely one-off external cause.

rules.rule: Incidents created by the same caller repeatedly for the same issue (unresolved root cause)
rules.what_it_means: The same caller raises repeated incidents for the same issue.
rules.why_it_matters: The underlying cause is not being resolved. Each incident is closed individually and the pattern is invisible because nothing aggregates across callers.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident caller, short description similarity, creation timing
rules.detection_logic: Caller and description-cluster pairs with repeat volume above threshold in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Similarity threshold and repeat count configurable
rules.evidence_to_show: Caller, the incident cluster, resolution codes used across them, and whether a Problem exists.
rules.false_positive_guard: Caller in a role that legitimately generates similar requests.

rules.rule: First-call resolution rate declining
rules.what_it_means: The first-call resolution rate is declining over time.
rules.why_it_matters: A capability or knowledge trend. Declining FCR with stable volume usually means knowledge is not keeping pace with the estate.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident resolution at first assignment, reassignment count, trend across windows
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(incidents resolved with zero reassignments) / COUNT(resolved), trended
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio. Trend confidence from window count.
rules.evidence_to_show: FCR trend overall and by group, with volume and category mix for context.
rules.false_positive_guard: Category mix shifted toward genuinely harder work.

rules.rule: Assignment to an individual rather than a group
rules.what_it_means: Incidents are assigned to an individual rather than to a group.
rules.why_it_matters: The ticket is invisible to the team and stalls when that person is unavailable. Creates key-person dependency in the queue.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident.assigned_to population without assignment_group, or assignment directly to individuals
rules.detection_logic: Incidents with assigned_to populated and assignment_group empty, or assignment patterns concentrated on individuals
rules.threshold_parameter: Report as a ratio and by individual
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio, distribution by individual, and the resolution time for individually assigned versus group assigned incidents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Specialist work where individual assignment is the operating model.

rules.rule: On-hold reason not captured
rules.what_it_means: The on-hold reason is not captured when incidents are placed on hold.
rules.why_it_matters: On-hold time is excluded from SLA and nobody knows why. Cannot distinguish legitimate vendor waits from parking, which makes ITSM-034 impossible to interpret.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident on-hold state transitions, hold reason field population
rules.detection_logic: On-hold transitions with empty hold reason
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio by group, the hold duration distribution, and the SLA pause time attributable to unreasoned holds.
rules.false_positive_guard: Hold reason captured in work notes instead.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — make the field mandatory on transition

rules.rule: Incidents resolved by the caller themselves
rules.what_it_means: Incidents are being resolved by the caller themselves.
rules.why_it_matters: Either the caller has fulfiller access they should not have, or resolution is being recorded under the wrong identity. The first is an access finding.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident caller_id and resolved_by comparison, caller role check
rules.detection_logic: Resolved incidents where caller_id equals resolved_by, joined to the caller's role set
rules.threshold_parameter: Report separately for callers with and without fulfiller roles
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by caller, their role set, the close codes used, and whether they hold fulfiller access.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate self-service resolution model.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3; escalate to access review where the caller should not have fulfiller roles

rules.rule: No major incident process configured despite P1 volume
rules.what_it_means: No major incident process is configured despite significant P1 volume.
rules.why_it_matters: Major incidents are being handled as ordinary P1s with no communication plan, no war room, no post-incident review and no structured escalation. The process that exists for the worst days does not exist.
rules.source_tables_fields: Major incident configuration, P1 volume, major incident record count
rules.detection_logic: P1 volume above threshold with zero or near-zero major incident records and no major incident configuration
rules.evidence_to_show: P1 volume, major incident record count, the configuration state, and the P1s that met major incident criteria by duration or impact.
rules.false_positive_guard: Major incident process run outside ServiceNow with documented evidence.
rules.cross_domain_link: Structural absence of the process that matters most

rules.rule: Major incident raised with no communication plan or task
rules.what_it_means: A major incident is raised with no communication plan or communication task.
rules.why_it_matters: During a major incident, stakeholder communication is the thing that fails first and is remembered longest. No plan means it depends on whoever thinks of it.
rules.source_tables_fields: Major incident records, communication plan and task linkage
rules.detection_logic: Major incidents with no communication plan record or communication task
rules.evidence_to_show: Major incident, duration, affected services, and the absence of communication records.
rules.false_positive_guard: Communication handled through an external mechanism with evidence.

rules.rule: Major incident closed with no post-incident review
rules.what_it_means: A major incident is closed with no post-incident review.
rules.why_it_matters: The most expensive learning opportunity the organisation gets, discarded. Guarantees the next occurrence starts from the same place.
rules.source_tables_fields: Major incident closure, PIR record linkage
rules.detection_logic: Closed major incidents with no linked post-incident review
rules.evidence_to_show: Major incident list, duration, business impact, and PIR linkage state.
rules.false_positive_guard: PIR conducted outside ServiceNow with evidence.

rules.rule: Major incident with no linked Problem record
rules.what_it_means: A major incident has no linked Problem record.
rules.why_it_matters: The specific version of ITSM-039 for the incidents that matter most. A major incident with no Problem is a decision not to find out why it happened.
rules.source_tables_fields: Major incident records, Problem linkage
rules.detection_logic: Major incidents with no linked Problem
rules.evidence_to_show: Major incident list with duration, affected services, close code, and Problem linkage state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Cause fully established during the incident and documented in the record.

rules.rule: Major incident with no affected service populated
rules.what_it_means: A major incident has no affected service populated.
rules.why_it_matters: The business impact of a major incident is unrecorded. Reporting to executives is anecdotal, and the incident cannot be aggregated into service reliability figures.
rules.source_tables_fields: Major incident business_service and affected service fields
rules.detection_logic: Major incidents with no service reference populated
rules.evidence_to_show: Major incident list, the CIs referenced, and whether those CIs have a traversable path to a service.
rules.false_positive_guard: Infrastructure-level incident with no single service impact.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the CI path resolves the service, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-057; often blocked by reachability

rules.rule: Major incident timeline gaps (no updates for extended periods)
rules.what_it_means: Major incident timelines contain gaps with no updates for extended periods.
rules.why_it_matters: The record does not reflect what happened. Post-incident review and any regulatory reporting work from an incomplete timeline.
rules.source_tables_fields: Major incident journal entries, update timestamps, gap analysis
rules.detection_logic: Major incidents with update gaps exceeding threshold during the active period
rules.threshold_parameter: Gap threshold default 30 minutes during an active major incident
rules.evidence_to_show: Major incident, its update timeline with gaps highlighted, duration, and the gap total as a share of incident duration.
rules.false_positive_guard: Updates captured in an external war-room channel.
rules.cross_domain_link: Post-incident review and regulatory evidence gap

rules.rule: Major incident candidate criteria never triggering
rules.what_it_means: Major incident candidate criteria are configured but never trigger.
rules.why_it_matters: The automatic promotion path does not work, so major incidents depend on a human deciding. Delays declaration, which is the most time-sensitive decision in the process.
rules.source_tables_fields: Major incident candidate rule configuration, trigger events, manual promotion records
rules.detection_logic: Candidate criteria configured with zero trigger events, where P1s meeting those criteria exist
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence with qualifying P1s present
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on trigger events and criteria evaluation.
rules.evidence_to_show: Criteria configuration, the P1s that met them, the trigger event absence, and the manual promotion timing for those incidents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Criteria deliberately advisory.

rules.rule: Post-incident review actions created but never closed
rules.what_it_means: Post-incident review actions are created and never closed.
rules.why_it_matters: The review happened, the actions were identified, and nothing was done. Worse than no review, because it creates a documented record of known risks left unaddressed.
rules.source_tables_fields: PIR action records, state and age
rules.detection_logic: Open PIR actions beyond age threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Action list with age, owner, source major incident, and whether that incident type has recurred since.
rules.false_positive_guard: Actions deliberately deferred with documented acceptance.

rules.rule: Problem process effectively unused — Problem-to-Incident ratio near zero
rules.what_it_means: The Problem process is effectively unused — the ratio of Problem records to incident volume is near zero.
rules.why_it_matters: Every incident is treated as a first occurrence. Recurring causes are resolved repeatedly at full cost and never removed. This is usually the single largest avoidable cost in an ITSM estate, and almost nobody measures it.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem record count, incident volume, ratio across the window
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(Problem records created) / COUNT(incidents created) in the window
rules.evidence_to_show: The ratio with trend, Problem creation by group, and the incident clusters that should have produced Problems.
rules.false_positive_guard: Problem management run outside ServiceNow with documented evidence.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — process adoption, not a data fix
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of repeated incident cost

rules.rule: Recurring incident patterns with no corresponding Problem record
rules.what_it_means: Recurring incident patterns exist with no corresponding Problem record.
rules.why_it_matters: Names the specific clusters rather than complaining about the ratio. Converts an abstract process criticism into a list of things to act on.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident short description and category clustering, Problem linkage
rules.detection_logic: Incident clusters above volume threshold with no linked Problem
rules.threshold_parameter: Cluster volume threshold and similarity threshold configurable
rules.confidence_basis: Clustering confidence from similarity score and volume. Report both.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ranked clusters with volume, total resolution effort, representative incidents, and Problem linkage state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Clusters representing genuinely distinct incidents with similar wording.

rules.rule: P1 and major incidents with no Problem raised
rules.what_it_means: P1 and major incidents have been closed with no Problem raised.
rules.why_it_matters: The highest-impact incidents are the ones least analysed. Each unanalysed major incident is a guaranteed repeat with no accumulated understanding.
rules.source_tables_fields: P1 and major incident records, Problem linkage
rules.detection_logic: P1 and major incidents closed with no linked Problem
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.evidence_to_show: Incident list with duration, affected services, business impact, and Problem linkage state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Cause established during the incident and documented.

rules.rule: Problem records created but never progressed past initial state
rules.what_it_means: Problem records are created and never progressed past their initial state.
rules.why_it_matters: The process is adopted in form and not in substance. Creating a Problem becomes a closure ritual for the incident rather than the start of analysis.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem state, creation date, state change audit
rules.detection_logic: Problems in the initial state beyond age threshold with no state change
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem list with age, creating group, linked incident count, and absence of state change.
rules.false_positive_guard: Problems deliberately parked pending a vendor.

rules.rule: Percentage of incident volume attributable to known problems
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of incident volume attributable to known problems.
rules.why_it_matters: The value measure for Problem management. A high number with open Problems means known causes are still generating cost; a high number with closed Problems means the fixes did not work.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident linkage to Problem and Known Error, incident volume
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(incidents linked to a Problem) / COUNT(incidents) in the window, split by Problem state
rules.threshold_parameter: Report by Problem state; no single threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio split by open and closed Problems, the top Problems by attributable incident volume, and the effort each represents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Linkage practice inconsistent, understating the true attribution.
rules.cross_domain_link: The business case for Problem management

rules.rule: Top ten incident clusters by short-description similarity with no Problem
rules.what_it_means: The top incident clusters by short-description similarity have no corresponding Problem.
rules.why_it_matters: The specific, ranked version of ITSM-054. This is the list to put in front of a Problem manager, because each entry carries a volume and an effort number.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident short_description clustering, resolution effort, Problem linkage
rules.detection_logic: Top N clusters by volume with no Problem link, ranked by aggregate resolution effort
rules.threshold_parameter: N default 10; effort derived from resolution time
rules.confidence_basis: Clustering confidence from similarity and volume, stated per cluster.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ranked clusters with volume, aggregate effort, representative incidents, the groups resolving them, and the close codes used.
rules.false_positive_guard: Clusters diluted by ITSM-023 template pasting. Report that finding alongside.
rules.cross_domain_link: The Problem management backlog, ranked by value

rules.rule: Problem raised only by one group (process not adopted estate-wide)
rules.what_it_means: Problem records are raised by only one group, indicating the process is not adopted across the estate.
rules.why_it_matters: One team practises Problem management and the rest do not. The measured Problem ratio looks better than reality because one group carries it.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem creation by group, incident volume by group
rules.detection_logic: Problem creation distribution by group, against incident volume distribution
rules.threshold_parameter: Flag where Problem creation concentration far exceeds incident concentration
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem creation by group, incident volume by group, and the ratio per group showing the adoption gap.
rules.false_positive_guard: Centralised Problem function by design.
rules.cross_domain_link: Adoption gap hidden by aggregate metrics

rules.rule: Problem records with no linked incidents
rules.what_it_means: Problem records exist with no linked incidents.
rules.why_it_matters: Either the linkage is not being done, in which case ITSM-057 understates attribution, or the Problem was raised speculatively with no evidence behind it.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem records, incident linkage
rules.detection_logic: Problems with zero linked incidents
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem list with state, age, creating group, and the incident clusters that match their description.
rules.false_positive_guard: Proactive Problems raised from monitoring or trend analysis rather than incidents.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where matching incidents can be identified, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Problems open beyond age threshold with no state change
rules.what_it_means: Problems are open beyond an age threshold with no state change.
rules.why_it_matters: Analysis stalled. The linked incidents continue to occur while the Problem sits, so the cost continues to accrue with no offsetting progress.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem state audit history, age
rules.detection_logic: Open Problems with no state change beyond age threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem list with age, last state change, owner, linked incident count, and incident volume accrued since the Problem opened.
rules.false_positive_guard: Problems awaiting a vendor fix with documented tracking.

rules.rule: Root cause field empty on closed Problems
rules.what_it_means: The root cause field is empty on closed Problems.
rules.why_it_matters: The Problem was closed without establishing why. Nothing was learned, the Known Error cannot be written, and the same cause will not be recognised next time.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem cause_notes or root cause field, closed Problems
rules.detection_logic: Closed Problems with empty root cause
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by group and close code, the linked incident volume for each, and the post-closure incident trend.
rules.false_positive_guard: Problems closed as duplicates or cancelled.

rules.rule: Workaround empty on Problems with open linked incidents
rules.what_it_means: The workaround field is empty on Problems that have open linked incidents.
rules.why_it_matters: Service desk agents have no interim guidance while the permanent fix is developed. Every linked incident is resolved from scratch.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem workaround field, linked incident state
rules.detection_logic: Problems with open linked incidents and empty workaround
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem list with open incident count, workaround state, and the average resolution time for linked incidents.
rules.false_positive_guard: No workaround genuinely exists.
rules.cross_domain_link: Direct cost in repeated resolution effort

rules.rule: Problem closed with no permanent fix and no accepted-risk decision
rules.what_it_means: A Problem is closed with no permanent fix recorded and no documented accepted-risk decision.
rules.why_it_matters: Closed without resolution and without a decision to accept it. The record says the Problem is dealt with and nothing changed.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem closure, fix and known error linkage, accepted risk field
rules.detection_logic: Closed Problems with no linked Change, no Known Error, and no accepted-risk record
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem list, closure code, linked artefacts, and the post-closure incident volume for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Fix implemented outside ServiceNow with evidence.

rules.rule: Problem with no assigned owner, or owner inactive
rules.what_it_means: A Problem has no assigned owner, or the owner is an inactive user.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody is progressing it. The Problem exists as a record with no path to resolution.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem assigned_to and assignment_group, sys_user.active, group membership
rules.detection_logic: Problems with empty owner, or owner resolving to an inactive user or empty group
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — resolves to an active person or does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem list with owner state, age, linked incident count, and last activity.
rules.false_positive_guard: Owner deactivated within a grace period with reassignment pending.

rules.rule: Known Error records not published to knowledge
rules.what_it_means: Known Error records are not published to the knowledge base.
rules.why_it_matters: The analysis exists and cannot be consumed. Agents resolving linked incidents cannot find the workaround that was written specifically for them.
rules.source_tables_fields: Known Error records, kb_knowledge linkage and publication state
rules.detection_logic: Known Errors with no published knowledge article, or with an article in draft
rules.evidence_to_show: Known Error list, article state, linked incident volume, and article view counts where published.
rules.false_positive_guard: Knowledge published in a separate system.

rules.rule: Problem not linked to a CI or service
rules.what_it_means: A Problem is not linked to a CI or a service.
rules.why_it_matters: The Problem cannot be aggregated by infrastructure or service. Recurring problems on the same CI are invisible as a pattern.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem cmdb_ci and business_service fields
rules.detection_logic: Problems with both CI and service references empty
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem list, linked incident CI distribution, and the CI the incidents point at.
rules.false_positive_guard: Problems concerning process rather than technology.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the linked incidents resolve the CI, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Problem tasks created but never completed
rules.what_it_means: Problem tasks are created and never completed.
rules.why_it_matters: The investigation was broken into steps and the steps were not done. The Problem appears active and is not progressing.
rules.source_tables_fields: Problem task records, state and age
rules.detection_logic: Open Problem tasks beyond age threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Task list with age, assignee, parent Problem, and the parent's state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Tasks deliberately sequenced with later start dates.

rules.rule: Problem closed while linked incidents remain open
rules.what_it_means: A Problem is closed while its linked incidents remain open.
rules.why_it_matters: The cause is declared resolved while the symptoms are still live. Either the closure is premature or the incidents should have been closed with it.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem state, linked incident states
rules.detection_logic: Closed Problems with one or more open linked incidents
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem, closure date and code, the open linked incidents with their ages, and their assignment groups.
rules.false_positive_guard: Incidents legitimately open for a separate reason.

rules.rule: Root cause text below meaningful length or restating the symptom
rules.what_it_means: Root cause text is below a meaningful length, or restates the symptom rather than the cause.
rules.why_it_matters: Passes any mandatory-field check while carrying no analysis. The Known Error written from it will be useless.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem root cause text length, similarity to the Problem description
rules.detection_logic: Closed Problems with root cause below length threshold, or similarity to description above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Length threshold default 40 characters; similarity threshold 0.85
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on length. 90% on the similarity check.
rules.evidence_to_show: Sample records with description and root cause, count by group, and the length distribution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely simple causes stated concisely.

rules.rule: Problem with no linked Change where a fix was clearly required
rules.what_it_means: A Problem has no linked Change where the root cause clearly required one.
rules.why_it_matters: The cause was identified, the fix required a change, and no change exists. Either the fix was implemented without change control, which is ITSM-106, or it was never implemented.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem records with root cause established, Change linkage, root cause classification
rules.detection_logic: Closed Problems with a root cause indicating a configuration or code fix, and no linked Change
rules.threshold_parameter: Root cause classification from close code and text pattern
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — the inference that a change was required is derived from the root cause classification.
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem, root cause, absence of Change linkage, and any unauthorised change detected on the related CI in the window.
rules.false_positive_guard: Fix applied through a standard change not linked back.

rules.rule: Problem state regressing repeatedly
rules.what_it_means: A Problem state regresses repeatedly, moving backward through the workflow more than once.
rules.why_it_matters: Analysis is being reopened repeatedly, which usually means the root cause was declared prematurely each time.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem state audit history, backward transitions
rules.detection_logic: Problems with more than N backward state transitions
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem, its state timeline, the backward transitions with users and dates, and the linked incident volume across the period.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate iterative investigation.

rules.rule: Problem priority not aligned to the aggregate impact of linked incidents
rules.what_it_means: Problem priority is not aligned to the aggregate impact of its linked incidents.
rules.why_it_matters: A Problem generating a thousand incidents sits at low priority while one generating five sits high. Problem prioritisation is disconnected from the cost it represents.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem priority, linked incident volume and priority distribution
rules.detection_logic: Problems whose priority is inconsistent with their linked incident aggregate volume and priority
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — the alignment expectation is encoded in configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem, its priority, linked incident volume and priority spread, and the aggregate resolution effort.
rules.false_positive_guard: Priority deliberately set on fix complexity rather than incident volume.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where realignment is unambiguous, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Incident volume for a resolved Problem not declining post-closure (fix ineffective)
rules.what_it_means: Incident volume for a resolved Problem has not declined after closure.
rules.why_it_matters: The fix did not work and nobody checked. The Problem is closed, the metric improved, and the cost continues unchanged. This is the only rule in the group that measures outcome rather than process.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem closure dates, linked incident volume before and after closure
rules.detection_logic: Linked incident rate in the N days after closure compared against the N days before
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 90 days either side. Flag where the decline is below threshold.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on volume comparison. Requires sufficient post-closure window; state it.
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem, closure date, incident volume trend before and after, and the permanent fix recorded.
rules.false_positive_guard: Insufficient time since closure. Do not evaluate before the full window has elapsed.
rules.cross_domain_link: The outcome measure for Problem management

rules.rule: Problem recurrence — same root cause appearing in multiple Problem records
rules.what_it_means: The same root cause appears across multiple separate Problem records.
rules.why_it_matters: The cause was identified more than once and resolved more than once, or not at all. Indicates either duplicate Problem creation or a fix that repeatedly fails.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem root cause text clustering across records
rules.detection_logic: Problem clusters by root cause similarity above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Similarity threshold default 0.8, minimum cluster size 2
rules.confidence_basis: Clustering confidence from similarity score. Report per cluster.
rules.evidence_to_show: The cluster, each Problem with its dates, closure state, permanent fix, and linked incident volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely similar but distinct causes on different systems.

rules.rule: Known Error articles with no views or no linkage from incidents
rules.what_it_means: Known Error articles have no views, or no linkage from incidents.
rules.why_it_matters: The knowledge exists and is not reaching agents. Either search is not surfacing it or the suggestion mechanism is not configured, which is ITSM-015.
rules.source_tables_fields: kb_knowledge view counts, incident-to-article linkage, Known Error records
rules.detection_logic: Known Error articles with zero views or zero incident linkage in the window
rules.evidence_to_show: Article list with views, linkage count, the incident volume that matched their topic, and the knowledge suggestion configuration state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Articles recently published with insufficient elapsed time.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 for the suggestion configuration, Lane 3 for content

rules.rule: Average time from incident cluster emergence to Problem creation
rules.what_it_means: The average time from incident cluster emergence to Problem creation.
rules.why_it_matters: Measures how long the organisation absorbs a recurring cost before recognising it. Every day in that interval is repeated resolution effort.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident cluster first occurrence, linked Problem creation date
rules.detection_logic: Mean and distribution of (Problem created - cluster first occurrence) across linked clusters
rules.threshold_parameter: Report distribution, not a single threshold
rules.confidence_basis: Cluster emergence date confidence from clustering quality.
rules.evidence_to_show: Distribution with the longest cases, the incident volume accrued during each interval, and the effort that represents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Clusters whose emergence is ambiguous.

rules.rule: Permanent fix implemented but no validation recorded
rules.what_it_means: A permanent fix is recorded as implemented with no validation recorded.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody confirmed the fix worked. Combined with ITSM-074, this is how ineffective fixes survive as closed Problems.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem fix records, validation fields, linked Change closure
rules.detection_logic: Problems with a permanent fix recorded and no validation entry or post-implementation review
rules.evidence_to_show: Problem, fix record, absence of validation, and the post-closure incident trend.
rules.false_positive_guard: Validation recorded in the linked Change instead.

rules.rule: Problems closed as "cannot reproduce" above threshold
rules.what_it_means: Problems closed as 'cannot reproduce' exceed a threshold share.
rules.why_it_matters: Sometimes legitimate, often a closure of convenience. A high rate concentrated in one group is a behavioural signal rather than a technical one.
rules.source_tables_fields: problem close codes, distribution by group
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(Problems closed as cannot reproduce) / COUNT(closed Problems), by group
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio by group, the linked incident volume for those Problems, and the post-closure incident trend.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely intermittent issues.

rules.rule: Standard change catalogue empty or unused — everything routed as Normal
rules.what_it_means: The standard change catalogue is empty or unused, so all work routes as Normal change.
rules.why_it_matters: Low-risk repeatable work carries full CAB overhead. Two consequences: the CAB spends its time on routine work rather than risk, and engineers route around the process because it is disproportionate.
rules.source_tables_fields: Standard change template records, change type distribution
rules.detection_logic: Standard change template count and usage against total change volume
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 20% of changes as standard for a mature estate
rules.evidence_to_show: Change type distribution, standard template count and usage, and the Normal changes with repeated identical descriptions that are standard-change candidates.
rules.false_positive_guard: Estate genuinely has no repeatable change patterns.
rules.cross_domain_link: Drives CAB overload and process avoidance

rules.rule: Approval routing with no defined approver group for a change type
rules.what_it_means: A change type has no defined approver group in its approval routing.
rules.why_it_matters: Changes of that type either bypass approval or hang indefinitely. Both outcomes are control failures, and which one occurs depends on workflow configuration nobody has checked.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change approval workflow configuration by type, approver group assignment
rules.detection_logic: Change types with volume but no configured approver group
rules.evidence_to_show: Change type, volume, approval configuration state, and the actual approval records for changes of that type.
rules.false_positive_guard: Type deliberately auto-approved with documented rationale.

rules.rule: CAB not configured, or CAB meeting workflow unused
rules.what_it_means: CAB is not configured, or the CAB meeting workflow exists and is unused.
rules.why_it_matters: There is no forum where change risk is collectively assessed. Approval becomes individual and asynchronous, which removes the cross-domain conflict detection that a CAB exists to provide.
rules.source_tables_fields: CAB configuration, CAB meeting records, change agenda linkage
rules.detection_logic: CAB configuration absent, or zero CAB meeting records in the window despite change volume
rules.evidence_to_show: CAB configuration state, meeting record count, change volume, and the approval mechanism actually in use.
rules.false_positive_guard: CAB conducted outside ServiceNow with documented evidence.

rules.rule: Risk assessment not configured, or risk always computed as the same value
rules.what_it_means: Risk assessment is not configured, or risk is computed as the same value for every change.
rules.why_it_matters: Risk stops differentiating. Every change carries the same assessment, so approval routing and scrutiny cannot vary by actual risk. Usually the risk questionnaire exists and nobody answers it.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change risk field distribution, risk assessment configuration and questionnaire completion
rules.detection_logic: Risk value distribution; flag where one value exceeds threshold share, or where risk assessment is unconfigured
rules.evidence_to_show: Risk distribution, the assessment configuration, questionnaire completion rate, and the correlation between assigned risk and actual change failure rate.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely homogeneous change portfolio.

rules.rule: No conflict detection configured
rules.what_it_means: No change conflict detection is configured.
rules.why_it_matters: Two changes can be approved for the same CI in the same window with nothing detecting the collision. The most common cause of change-induced incidents is two changes nobody knew about each other.
rules.source_tables_fields: Conflict detection configuration, change schedule overlap analysis
rules.detection_logic: Conflict detection unconfigured, or configured with zero detections despite overlapping changes existing
rules.threshold_parameter: Report both cases; the second is ITSM-138
rules.evidence_to_show: Configuration state, the overlapping changes that existed and were not detected, and the incidents that followed them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Conflict managed manually through the CAB with evidence.

rules.rule: Blackout and maintenance windows not defined
rules.what_it_means: Blackout and maintenance windows are not defined.
rules.why_it_matters: There is no mechanism to prevent change during periods when change should not happen. Quarter-end, peak trading, regulatory reporting windows are all unprotected.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_schedule blackout and maintenance window definitions, change activity distribution
rules.detection_logic: Absence of blackout or maintenance window definitions where change volume exists
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule configuration state, change volume distribution by date, and any change activity during known sensitive periods.
rules.false_positive_guard: Windows managed through a separate calendar with evidence.

rules.rule: Emergency change path with the same approval requirements as Normal (so it gets bypassed)
rules.what_it_means: The emergency change path carries the same approval burden as a Normal change.
rules.why_it_matters: The emergency path exists to move fast under control. If it is no faster, it gets bypassed entirely and emergency work happens with no record at all, which is worse than either alternative.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change type approval configuration, approval step counts and turnaround by type
rules.detection_logic: Emergency change approval step count and turnaround compared against Normal
rules.threshold_parameter: Flag where emergency approval burden is not materially lighter
rules.evidence_to_show: Approval configuration by type, step counts, actual turnaround distribution, and the unauthorised change rate for comparison.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate design with a documented fast-track mechanism elsewhere.

rules.rule: Change model states allowing closure without implementation evidence
rules.what_it_means: The change model permits closure without any implementation evidence recorded.
rules.why_it_matters: Changes close as Successful with nothing to show they were implemented. Audit has no evidence trail, and post-implementation review has nothing to review.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change state model, closure requirements, close notes and implementation evidence population
rules.detection_logic: Change models allowing closure with empty close notes and no implementation evidence fields required
rules.evidence_to_show: Model configuration, closure requirements, and the proportion of closed changes with no implementation evidence.
rules.false_positive_guard: Evidence captured in an external deployment system with linkage.

rules.rule: Approval delegation configured to inactive users
rules.what_it_means: Approval delegation is configured to inactive users.
