rules.why_it_matters: Delegated approvals route to nobody. Changes hang, and the workaround is usually to bypass approval, which becomes ITSM-106.
rules.source_tables_fields: Approval delegation configuration, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Active delegations whose delegate resolves to an inactive user
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — resolves to an active user or does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Delegation record, delegator, delegate state, and the approvals currently hanging on it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Delegate deactivated within a grace period.

rules.rule: Standard change templates with no expiry or review date
rules.what_it_means: Standard change templates have no expiry or review date.
rules.why_it_matters: A standard change is pre-approved because the risk was assessed once. Without review, that assessment ages indefinitely while the environment changes underneath it.
rules.source_tables_fields: Standard change template records, expiry and review date fields
rules.detection_logic: Standard templates with no expiry or review date, or past review date
rules.threshold_parameter: Review period from policy; default 12 months
rules.evidence_to_show: Template list with creation date, last review, usage volume, and the change success rate for changes raised from each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Templates under a documented external review cycle.
rules.cross_domain_link: Pre-approval based on an ageing assessment

rules.rule: Risk matrix fields not mandatory
rules.what_it_means: Risk matrix input fields are not mandatory.
rules.why_it_matters: Risk can be computed from an incomplete assessment, or defaulted. Produces ITSM-083 as a downstream effect.
rules.source_tables_fields: Risk assessment field mandatory configuration, field population rates
rules.detection_logic: Risk matrix input fields with no mandatory enforcement and population rate below threshold
rules.evidence_to_show: Field list, mandatory state, population rate, and the resulting risk value distribution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Risk assessed through a questionnaire with its own enforcement.

rules.rule: Change types customised without corresponding approval logic
rules.what_it_means: Custom change types have been created without corresponding approval logic.
rules.why_it_matters: The type exists, changes are raised against it, and no approval workflow covers it. A control gap created by configuration rather than by bypass.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change type choices vs OOB set, approval workflow coverage by type
rules.detection_logic: Custom change types with volume and no matching approval workflow condition
rules.threshold_parameter: Any custom type with non-zero volume
rules.evidence_to_show: Custom type, volume, approval workflow coverage, and the actual approval records for changes of that type.
rules.false_positive_guard: Type covered by a general workflow condition.

rules.rule: No post-implementation review step for high-risk changes
rules.what_it_means: There is no post-implementation review step configured for high-risk changes.
rules.why_it_matters: High-risk changes are implemented and never reviewed. Whether they achieved their objective, and what they broke, is never established.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change model PIR configuration by risk band, PIR record existence
rules.detection_logic: High-risk change types with no PIR step configured, or zero PIR records for high-risk changes
rules.evidence_to_show: Configuration state by risk band, high-risk change volume, PIR record count, and the incident rate following high-risk changes.
rules.false_positive_guard: PIR conducted through a separate process.

rules.rule: Change calendar not published or not consumed
rules.what_it_means: The change calendar is not published, or is published and not consumed.
rules.why_it_matters: Teams cannot see what else is happening. Conflict detection catches technical collisions; the calendar catches the human ones, and without it nobody knows a related change is in flight.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change calendar configuration and publication, calendar view access logs where available
rules.detection_logic: Calendar unconfigured or unpublished, or published with negligible access
rules.threshold_parameter: Access threshold where log data is available
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration. Consumption depends on access log availability.
rules.evidence_to_show: Calendar configuration state, publication, access volume, and the change volume it would cover.
rules.false_positive_guard: Calendar consumed through an exported feed.

rules.rule: Percentage of changes with no CI and no service reference
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of changes referencing neither a CI nor a service.
rules.why_it_matters: Conflict detection, risk assessment and impact analysis all key off the CI reference. Without it, none of them can run, so the change is approved on narrative alone.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request.cmdb_ci and business_service, change volume
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(changes with both fields empty) / COUNT(changes) in the window
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio trend, distribution by type and group, and the conflict detection results for changes with and without CI references.
rules.false_positive_guard: Change types where no CI is meaningful, such as process or documentation changes.
rules.cross_domain_link: Makes ITSM-084 and ITSM-138 structurally impossible

rules.rule: Change referencing a retired or non-existent CI
rules.what_it_means: A change references a CI that is retired or does not exist.
rules.why_it_matters: The change targets infrastructure that officially does not exist. Conflict detection and impact analysis traverse from a dead record and return nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request.cmdb_ci, cmdb_ci existence and lifecycle
rules.detection_logic: Changes referencing a CI sys_id with no record, or a CI in a retired state
rules.evidence_to_show: Change list, the referenced CI and its state, and the live CI the change probably concerns.
rules.false_positive_guard: Change raised specifically to complete a decommission.

rules.rule: Implementation plan empty
rules.what_it_means: The implementation plan is empty.
rules.why_it_matters: The approver is approving an unspecified action. There is no basis on which to assess risk, and no record of what was supposed to happen if it goes wrong.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request implementation plan field
rules.detection_logic: Approved or closed changes with empty implementation plan
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report by type and risk band
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by type, risk band and group, with the approval records showing what was approved without a plan.
rules.false_positive_guard: Standard changes where the template carries the plan.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — mandatory enforcement at the approval state

rules.rule: Backout plan empty
rules.what_it_means: The backout plan is empty.
rules.why_it_matters: When the change fails, there is no documented way back. The recovery is improvised during an incident, which is the worst possible time to design it.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request backout plan field
rules.detection_logic: Approved or closed changes with empty backout plan
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; escalate for high-risk and production changes
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by risk band and type, the failed changes among them, and the recovery time for those failures.
rules.false_positive_guard: Standard changes where the template carries the backout.

rules.rule: Test plan empty on high-risk changes
rules.what_it_means: The test plan is empty on high-risk changes.
rules.why_it_matters: High-risk change proceeding with no defined verification. Whether it worked is established by whether something breaks.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request test plan field, risk band
rules.detection_logic: High-risk changes with empty test plan
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by risk band and group, the change success rate for these versus those with test plans.
rules.false_positive_guard: Testing evidenced in a linked external record.
rules.cross_domain_link: No defined verification on the riskiest work

rules.rule: Risk and impact fields unpopulated
rules.what_it_means: Risk and impact fields are unpopulated.
rules.why_it_matters: The change carries no assessment at all. Approval routing that keys off risk cannot function, so it defaults, usually to the lightest path.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request risk and impact fields
rules.detection_logic: Changes with risk or impact unpopulated at approval
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by type and group, the approval path taken for each, and the change success rate.
rules.false_positive_guard: Types where risk is inherited from the template.
rules.cross_domain_link: Approval routing defaults to the lightest path

rules.rule: Planned start and end dates absent or in the past at approval
rules.what_it_means: Planned start and end dates are absent, or are in the past at the point of approval.
rules.why_it_matters: A change with no window cannot be conflict-checked, cannot be calendared, and cannot be verified as implemented within its approval. Past dates at approval indicate retrospective raising.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request planned start and end dates, approval timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Changes with empty planned dates at approval, or planned start earlier than approval date
rules.threshold_parameter: Report the two cases separately; the second feeds ITSM-108
rules.evidence_to_show: Change list with planned dates, approval date, actual implementation date, and the gap.
rules.false_positive_guard: Emergency changes approved after the fact under a documented emergency process.
rules.cross_domain_link: Feeds ITSM-108 and blocks conflict detection

rules.rule: Assignment group with zero active members
rules.what_it_means: A change is assigned to a group with zero active members.
rules.why_it_matters: The implementation has no owner. The change sits in a queue nobody sees until the planned window passes.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request.assignment_group, sys_user_grmember, sys_user.active
rules.detection_logic: Open changes whose assignment group resolves to zero active members
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — resolves to a person or does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change count by group, their planned windows, risk bands, and the empty groups with last membership change date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Group emptied with reassignment in progress.
rules.cross_domain_link: Cross-links to CMDB-102 and Data Quality Q2

rules.rule: Justification or business reason empty
rules.what_it_means: The justification or business reason field is empty.
rules.why_it_matters: The change has no recorded purpose. Audit cannot establish why it was made, and post-implementation review cannot assess whether it achieved anything.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request justification or business reason field
rules.detection_logic: Approved or closed changes with empty justification
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by type, group and risk band, with the approval records.
rules.false_positive_guard: Justification carried in the linked incident or problem.

rules.rule: Change closed with no close code or close notes
rules.what_it_means: A change is closed with no close code or close notes.
rules.why_it_matters: Whether the change succeeded is unrecorded. The change success rate, which is the primary quality measure for the process, is computed over incomplete data.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request close_code and close_notes on closed changes
rules.detection_logic: Closed changes with empty close code or close notes
rules.evidence_to_show: Count by type and group, and the change success rate computed with and without these records.
rules.false_positive_guard: Closure via an automated integration not populating the fields.

rules.rule: Backout plan text identical across many changes (template pasting)
rules.what_it_means: Backout plan text is identical across a large number of changes.
rules.why_it_matters: Template pasting. The field is populated, the control appears satisfied, and no change has a backout plan specific to what it is actually doing.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request backout plan text frequency distribution
rules.detection_logic: Backout plan values appearing above a volume threshold, normalised
rules.threshold_parameter: Volume threshold configurable relative to change volume
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on frequency. The template-pasting interpretation is inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Repeated text with volume, the groups producing it, and the change types involved.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately identical backout for a genuinely repeatable standard change.

rules.rule: Affected CI list containing a single CI where the change clearly spans more
rules.what_it_means: The affected CI list contains a single CI where the change clearly spans more.
rules.why_it_matters: Under-declared scope. Conflict detection and impact analysis run against a fraction of what the change touches, so both return falsely reassuring results.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request affected CI list, CI relationship traversal from the primary CI
rules.detection_logic: Changes with a single affected CI whose description or type indicates broader scope, or whose primary CI has dependent CIs not declared
rules.threshold_parameter: Scope inference from change type and CI relationship depth
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — scope inference is the weakest rule in this group. Report with the relationship evidence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, declared CI, the dependent CIs not declared, and the conflict detection result with and without them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Change genuinely scoped to one CI.

rules.rule: Unauthorised change rate — CI modified with no corresponding approved change
rules.what_it_means: CIs have been modified with no corresponding approved change record.
rules.why_it_matters: The change control process was bypassed. For a regulated entity this is the most consequential finding in the ITSM catalogue, because it is a direct audit exception rather than a quality observation.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci and configuration object audit history, change_request records and windows, CI-to-change correlation
rules.detection_logic: Configuration modifications on change-controlled objects with no approved change covering the object and timestamp
rules.threshold_parameter: Scope to change-controlled object classes; correlation window configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — attribution depends on audit completeness and on change records carrying accurate CI references. Where ITSM-094 is high, this rule understates.
rules.evidence_to_show: The modification with object, timestamp and user, the absence of a covering change, and the approved changes in the window for comparison.
rules.false_positive_guard: Change raised without a CI reference, so the correlation fails. Report ITSM-094 alongside and state the understatement.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — this is an audit finding, not a data fix
rules.cross_domain_link: The headline control integrity finding; route to audit

rules.rule: Emergency change ratio above threshold (emergency used to bypass control)
rules.what_it_means: The emergency change ratio exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: Emergency exists to handle genuine urgency. A high ratio means it is being used to avoid the Normal approval path, which converts a control into a formality.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request type distribution, emergency change volume
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(emergency changes) / COUNT(all changes), overall and by group and approver
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio overall, by group and by approver, with the emergency justifications and the approval turnaround for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: A period of genuine operational crisis.
rules.cross_domain_link: Control integrity; concentration by approver is the strongest signal

rules.rule: Retrospective change rate — changes raised after implementation
rules.what_it_means: Changes are being raised after they have already been implemented.
rules.why_it_matters: The record is created to satisfy the process rather than to control the work. Approval is retrospective and therefore meaningless as a control.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request creation timestamp, planned and actual start, CI modification timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Changes whose creation or approval timestamp postdates the actual implementation evidence
rules.threshold_parameter: Correlation against CI audit where available; otherwise against actual start field
rules.confidence_basis: 95% where CI audit corroborates. 80% where only the actual start field is available.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, creation and approval timestamps, actual implementation evidence and its timestamp, and the gap.
rules.false_positive_guard: Emergency changes raised retrospectively under a documented emergency process.

rules.rule: Self-approval — requester and approver the same person
rules.what_it_means: The requester and the approver on a change are the same person.
rules.why_it_matters: A segregation of duties failure. One person authorised their own work. In a regulated entity this is an audit exception regardless of whether the change was appropriate.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request requested_by, approval records approver
rules.detection_logic: Changes where an approval record's approver equals the requester
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, requester, approver, approval timestamp, risk band, and the affected CIs.
rules.false_positive_guard: Documented single-person authority for a defined low-risk category with compensating controls.
rules.cross_domain_link: Segregation of duties failure; route to audit

rules.rule: Approval granted outside the approver's authority level
rules.what_it_means: Approval was granted by someone outside the authority level required for that change's risk band.
rules.why_it_matters: The approval exists and was not valid. Subtler than self-approval and equally consequential, because the control appears satisfied on the record.
rules.source_tables_fields: Approval records, approver role and authority configuration, change risk band
rules.detection_logic: Approvals where the approver's authority level is below that required for the change risk band
rules.threshold_parameter: Authority matrix from the customer's own delegation policy
rules.confidence_basis: 100% where an authority matrix exists. Where none exists, report that absence instead.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, risk band, required authority, the approver and their actual authority, and the approval record.
rules.false_positive_guard: Delegated authority not reflected in the role configuration.
rules.cross_domain_link: Control integrity; requires the authority matrix to detect

rules.rule: Change implemented outside its approved window
rules.what_it_means: A change was implemented outside its approved window.
rules.why_it_matters: What was approved and what happened are different. Conflict detection and calendar protection were both computed against the approved window and do not apply to the actual one.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request planned start and end, actual start and end, or CI modification timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Changes whose actual implementation falls outside the approved planned window beyond tolerance
rules.confidence_basis: 95% where actual timestamps are populated; 90% where inferred from CI audit.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, approved window, actual implementation window, the deviation, and any conflicting change in the actual window.
rules.false_positive_guard: Window extended through a documented approval amendment.
rules.cross_domain_link: Invalidates conflict detection and calendar protection

rules.rule: Change implemented during a blackout period
rules.what_it_means: A change was implemented during a defined blackout period.
rules.why_it_matters: The blackout existed to protect a period the business identified as sensitive, and it was crossed. The most directly reportable control breach in the change catalogue.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request implementation timestamps, cmn_schedule blackout definitions
rules.detection_logic: Changes whose implementation window intersects a defined blackout period
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires blackout windows to be defined; report ITSM-085 where they are not
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on window intersection where blackouts are defined.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, implementation window, the blackout period it crossed, the approver, and any override justification.
rules.false_positive_guard: Documented blackout exception approved in advance.

rules.rule: Change success rate below threshold
rules.what_it_means: The change success rate is below threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: The primary quality measure for change management. Only meaningful alongside ITSM-103 and ITSM-115, because closure codes are frequently inaccurate.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request close codes, closed change volume
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(changes closed successful) / COUNT(closed changes), by type, risk band and group
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio, conditional on close code accuracy. Report ITSM-103 and ITSM-115 alongside.
rules.evidence_to_show: Success rate by type, risk band and group, with the trend and the incident rate following changes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Close codes unreliable, overstating success. Report the qualifying findings.
rules.cross_domain_link: Requires ITSM-103 and ITSM-115 to interpret

rules.rule: Failed change rate with no corresponding backout executed
rules.what_it_means: Changes failed with no corresponding backout executed.
rules.why_it_matters: The change failed and the environment was left in the failed state. Either the backout plan was not usable or nobody executed it, and in both cases the recovery was improvised.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request close codes indicating failure, backout execution records or task closure
rules.detection_logic: Failed changes with no backout task completed or backout evidence recorded
rules.evidence_to_show: Failed change list, backout plan content, backout execution evidence, and the incidents raised following each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Backout not required because the change did not reach a state needing reversal.

rules.rule: Changes closed as Successful with a linked incident created within the window
rules.what_it_means: Changes closed as Successful have a linked incident created within the post-implementation window.
rules.why_it_matters: The change is recorded as successful and caused an incident. The success rate is overstated by exactly this population, which is why ITSM-113 cannot be read alone.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request closure, incident creation timestamps and CI correlation, post-implementation window
rules.detection_logic: Successful changes with an incident on the same or dependent CI within the window after implementation
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 72 hours. CI correlation includes dependent CIs where relationships exist.
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — correlation by CI and timing is strong but circumstantial without an explicit link.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, closure code, the correlated incident with its timing and CI, and the corrected success rate.
rules.false_positive_guard: Coincidental incident unrelated to the change.

rules.rule: Approval turnaround near-zero (rubber-stamping)
rules.what_it_means: Approval turnaround is near zero — approvals granted within seconds or minutes of request.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody read it. The approval control is executing and producing no scrutiny, which is indistinguishable from no control at all from a risk perspective.
rules.source_tables_fields: Approval records, request and approval timestamps, distribution by approver
rules.detection_logic: Approvals with turnaround below threshold, grouped by approver and change type
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 120 seconds. Report the distribution, not only the outliers.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on timestamp arithmetic. The interpretation is inferred and should be stated as such.
rules.evidence_to_show: Turnaround distribution by approver, the sub-threshold population, the risk bands involved, and each approver's total volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Approvals genuinely pre-discussed in a CAB and formalised afterwards.
rules.cross_domain_link: Control integrity; concentration by approver is the signal

rules.rule: Standard change used for work that meets Normal change criteria
rules.what_it_means: Standard change is being used for work that meets Normal change criteria.
rules.why_it_matters: The pre-approval was granted for a defined low-risk activity and is being applied to something else. The scrutiny that the work required was bypassed by template selection.
rules.source_tables_fields: Standard change template scope, actual change content and affected CIs, risk indicators
rules.detection_logic: Standard changes whose affected CIs, risk indicators or description fall outside the template scope
rules.threshold_parameter: Template scope from the template definition
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — scope comparison depends on template definitions being specific enough to compare against.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, the template used, its defined scope, the actual scope, and the risk indicators that would have applied under Normal.
rules.false_positive_guard: Template scope defined broadly and legitimately covering the work.

rules.rule: Conflict detected but overridden with no justification
rules.what_it_means: A conflict was detected and overridden with no justification recorded.
rules.why_it_matters: The control worked, the warning was given, and it was dismissed silently. Nobody can establish why the risk was accepted.
rules.source_tables_fields: Conflict detection results, override records, justification field
rules.detection_logic: Detected conflicts with an override and no justification text
rules.evidence_to_show: Conflict, the changes involved, the override user and timestamp, and any incident that followed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Justification recorded in work notes rather than the field.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — make justification mandatory on override

rules.rule: Change with no linked incident or problem and no business justification
rules.what_it_means: A change has no linked incident or problem and no business justification.
rules.why_it_matters: The change has no traceable origin. It was made because someone decided to, with no recorded demand behind it.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request incident and problem linkage, justification field
rules.detection_logic: Changes with no linked incident, no linked problem, and empty justification
rules.evidence_to_show: Change list by type and group, with the affected CIs and the approval records.
rules.false_positive_guard: Proactive maintenance or project work with justification held in a linked project record.

rules.rule: Changes repeatedly rescheduled
rules.what_it_means: Changes are repeatedly rescheduled.
rules.why_it_matters: Each reschedule invalidates the conflict detection and calendar position computed for the prior window. Frequent rescheduling also suggests the planning is not realistic.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request planned date audit history, reschedule count
rules.detection_logic: Changes with more than N planned date changes
rules.evidence_to_show: Change list with reschedule count and timeline, the groups involved, and whether conflict detection was re-run after each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate rescheduling due to external dependency.

rules.rule: Approvals by a single approver across a disproportionate share of changes
rules.what_it_means: A single approver accounts for a disproportionate share of all change approvals.
rules.why_it_matters: Concentration risk and a scrutiny risk. One person cannot meaningfully assess a very high volume, which is usually confirmed by their turnaround distribution.
rules.source_tables_fields: Approval records by approver, total approval volume
rules.detection_logic: Approvers holding more than threshold share of total approvals
rules.evidence_to_show: Approval distribution by approver, the top approvers with volume, and their turnaround distribution for cross-reference against ITSM-116.
rules.false_positive_guard: A designated change authority role with a deliberate concentration.
rules.cross_domain_link: Pairs with ITSM-116; concentration plus fast turnaround is the strong finding

rules.rule: Change closed without post-implementation review where required
rules.what_it_means: A change is closed without the post-implementation review that its risk band requires.
rules.why_it_matters: The review requirement exists and is not enforced at closure. High-risk changes complete with no assessment of outcome.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request closure, PIR requirement by risk band, PIR record linkage
rules.detection_logic: Closed changes in risk bands requiring PIR with no linked PIR record
rules.evidence_to_show: Change list by risk band, PIR requirement, linkage state, and the incident rate following them.
rules.false_positive_guard: PIR conducted through a separate process with evidence.
rules.cross_domain_link: No outcome assessment on high-risk change

rules.rule: Percentage of P1 incidents preceded by a change on the same CI within the window
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of P1 incidents preceded by a change on the same or a dependent CI within the correlation window.
rules.why_it_matters: The single most useful number in change management. It converts an abstract quality discussion into a measured statement about how much of the worst operational impact is self-inflicted.
rules.source_tables_fields: P1 incidents with CI references, change_request implementation windows, CI relationship traversal
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(P1 incidents with a preceding change on the same or dependent CI in the window) / COUNT(P1 incidents with a CI reference)
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 72 hours. Dependent CI traversal depth default 2.
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — correlation by CI and timing is strong but circumstantial. State the window and the traversal depth with the number.
rules.evidence_to_show: The ratio, the correlated pairs with timings, the change types and groups involved, and the resolution codes on the incidents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Coincidental timing. Requires ITSM-094 to be low, or the denominator is unreliable.
rules.cross_domain_link: The headline change-quality measure; depends on CMDB relationships to compute

rules.rule: Change-induced incident rate by group, by type, by CI class
rules.what_it_means: The change-induced incident rate, broken down by group, change type and CI class.
rules.why_it_matters: The actionable form of ITSM-123. Tells you which team, which change type and which infrastructure class produce the failures, rather than that failures occur.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change-incident correlation results, grouped by dimension
rules.detection_logic: Correlated incident count / change count, by group, by type, and by CI class
rules.threshold_parameter: Same window and traversal parameters as ITSM-123
rules.evidence_to_show: Rate by each dimension, ranked, with volume so small-sample noise is visible.
rules.false_positive_guard: Small sample sizes producing unstable rates. Enforce a minimum volume per dimension.
rules.cross_domain_link: Directs remediation effort to the specific source

rules.rule: CIs with a repeated change-then-incident pattern
rules.what_it_means: Specific CIs show a repeated change-then-incident pattern.
rules.why_it_matters: Names the infrastructure that breaks whenever it is touched. Usually indicates undocumented complexity or missing test coverage on that specific component.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change-incident correlation by CI, repeat count
rules.detection_logic: CIs with more than N correlated change-incident pairs in the window
rules.confidence_basis: Inherits correlation confidence; repetition strengthens it materially.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI, the correlated pairs with dates, the change types involved, the incidents, and whether a Problem exists for the CI.
rules.false_positive_guard: High-change-volume CI where the absolute count is expected.  Normalise by change volume.
rules.cross_domain_link: Identifies fragile infrastructure; strong Problem candidate

rules.rule: Changes to CIs supporting Business Critical services with no service reference populated
rules.what_it_means: Changes to CIs supporting Business Critical services have no service reference populated.
rules.why_it_matters: The change record does not say it affects a critical service. Approval routing, notification and impact assessment all proceed as if it were routine.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request CI references, CI-to-service traversal, business_service field
rules.detection_logic: Changes whose affected CIs traverse to a Business Critical service, with business_service empty
rules.confidence_basis: 100% where the traversal resolves. Depends on CMDB relationship completeness.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, its CI, the traversal path to the critical service, and the approval path taken versus the path that criticality would have required.
rules.false_positive_guard: Traversal resolving a service the change does not genuinely affect.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — populate the service reference from the traversal, reversible
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-057; changes approved without known criticality

rules.rule: Change freeze periods with change activity anyway
rules.what_it_means: Change activity occurred during a defined change freeze period.
rules.why_it_matters: Broader than ITSM-112, covering organisational freeze periods as well as technical blackouts. The freeze was a business decision and it was not honoured.
rules.source_tables_fields: Change implementation timestamps, freeze period definitions
rules.detection_logic: Changes implemented during a defined freeze, by type and approver
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires freeze periods to be defined
rules.evidence_to_show: Freeze period, the changes implemented in it with types and approvers, and any freeze exception approvals.
rules.false_positive_guard: Documented freeze exceptions approved in advance.

rules.rule: Incidents resolved with a resolution code indicating change causation, but no change linked
rules.what_it_means: Incidents are resolved with a resolution code indicating change causation, but no change is linked.
rules.why_it_matters: The service desk identified the cause as a change and the linkage was never made. ITSM-123 understates by exactly this population.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident close codes indicating change causation, change linkage
rules.detection_logic: Incidents with a change-causation close code and no linked change
rules.evidence_to_show: Incident list with close code, the changes in the preceding window on the same CI, and the linkage absence.
rules.false_positive_guard: Close code applied loosely.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the correlated change is unambiguous, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.rule: Incident, Problem and Change all failing to reference the CMDB — the three processes operating blind
rules.what_it_means: Incident, Problem and Change are all failing to reference the CMDB at material rates simultaneously.
rules.why_it_matters: The three core processes are operating blind. Not three separate data quality findings — one structural statement that the CMDB is not part of how this organisation works, which reframes every CMDB investment conversation.
rules.source_tables_fields: CI and service reference rates across incident, problem and change_request
rules.detection_logic: Reference rates below threshold across all three processes simultaneously
rules.threshold_parameter: Per-process thresholds; fires only when all three breach
rules.evidence_to_show: Reference rate for each process side by side, trended, with the CMDB Trust Score for context.
rules.false_positive_guard: Processes deliberately operating without CMDB linkage.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 across all three, plus Lane 3 process adoption
rules.cross_domain_link: The structural statement that frames the whole assessment

rules.rule: Incident volume on CIs with no relationships (impact analysis structurally impossible)
rules.what_it_means: Incident volume is concentrated on CIs that have no relationships, making impact analysis structurally impossible for those incidents.
rules.why_it_matters: The incidents that occur most are on the CIs the model knows least about. Every one of them is triaged without impact context, and no amount of process improvement changes that.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident CI references, cmdb_rel_ci edge counts for those CIs
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(incidents on CIs with zero edges) / COUNT(incidents with a CI reference)
rules.evidence_to_show: The ratio, the CIs involved ranked by incident volume, their edge counts, and the services they should connect to.
rules.false_positive_guard: CI classes that legitimately have no relationships.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — relationship restoration for the highest-volume CIs first
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-058; prioritises relationship remediation by incident volume

rules.rule: Change risk assessment computed without CMDB dependency data
rules.what_it_means: Change risk assessment is being computed without CMDB dependency data, because the affected CIs have no relationships to traverse.
rules.why_it_matters: The risk score is produced from the questionnaire alone. It cannot account for what the change actually touches, so a change to a core dependency scores the same as one to an isolated server.
rules.source_tables_fields: change_request risk values, affected CI relationship depth, risk calculation configuration
rules.detection_logic: Changes whose risk was computed where the affected CIs have zero or minimal relationship depth
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the join between risk computation and CI edge state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Change, assigned risk, affected CI edge counts, the dependency depth available, and the change failure rate for these versus dependency-rich changes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Risk model that deliberately does not use dependency data.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 for relationships, Lane 2 for the risk model
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-058; risk assessment computed on absent data

rules.rule: Recurring incidents on CIs whose CMDB data is stale, traced to a discovery failure
rules.what_it_means: Recurring incidents are occurring on CIs whose CMDB data is stale, traced to a specific discovery failure.
rules.why_it_matters: The full chain in one finding: a discovery failure produced stale CIs, the stale CIs cannot support impact analysis or accurate routing, and the incidents on them recur. Connects an ITOM configuration defect directly to operational cost.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident recurrence by CI, cmdb_ci.last_discovered, ITOM discovery failure attribution
rules.detection_logic: Recurring incident clusters on CIs whose staleness traces to an identified discovery failure
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires the ITOM cause to be identified; links to ITOM-147
rules.confidence_basis: Correlation confidence from the strength of the ITOM attribution. State the chain.
rules.evidence_to_show: The CIs, their staleness and its ITOM cause, the recurring incidents with volume and effort, and the resolution codes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Recurrence unrelated to the data staleness.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — fix the ITOM cause first
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins ITOM-147 and CMDB-072 to operational cost

rules.rule: Business Critical service with high incident volume and no Problem records
rules.what_it_means: A Business Critical service carries high incident volume and has no Problem records.
rules.why_it_matters: The services that matter most are absorbing repeated failure with no analysis. The most defensible Problem management finding available, because it names services the business recognises.
rules.source_tables_fields: Service criticality, incident volume by service, Problem linkage by service
rules.detection_logic: Business Critical services with incident volume above threshold and zero linked Problems
rules.threshold_parameter: Volume threshold relative to the service population
rules.evidence_to_show: Service, criticality, incident volume and trend, aggregate resolution effort, and Problem linkage state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Problems raised against the CIs rather than the service.
rules.cross_domain_link: The Problem management finding to put in front of an executive

rules.rule: Assignment groups referenced across all three processes with zero active members
rules.what_it_means: The same assignment groups with zero active members appear across incident, problem and change.
rules.why_it_matters: One broken group affecting all three processes. Demonstrates that group membership is a shared dependency, and that a single Data Quality defect propagates across the entire operating model.
rules.source_tables_fields: Assignment group references across all three task tables, group active membership
rules.detection_logic: Groups with zero active members referenced by open records in more than one process
rules.evidence_to_show: Group, active membership, the open records in each process referencing it, their ages and priorities.
rules.false_positive_guard: Group in transition with reassignment in progress.
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-102, ITSM-018, ITSM-101 and Data Quality Q2

rules.rule: CI owner and incident assignment group inconsistent
rules.what_it_means: The CI owner and the incident assignment group for incidents on that CI are inconsistent.
rules.why_it_matters: Two different groups believe they are accountable, or neither does. During escalation this produces the delay that the CMDB ownership field exists to prevent.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_ci ownership fields, incident assignment_group distribution per CI
rules.detection_logic: CIs whose owner or support group differs from the dominant incident assignment group for that CI
rules.threshold_parameter: Dominance threshold configurable; requires minimum incident volume per CI
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — divergence is a signal, not proof that either is wrong.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI, its recorded ownership, the actual incident assignment distribution, and the reassignment rate for those incidents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate separation of CI ownership from incident response.
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-106; ownership data contradicted by behaviour

rules.rule: Service referenced in incidents but absent from the CSDM model
rules.what_it_means: Services referenced in incidents do not exist in the CSDM model.
rules.why_it_matters: The service desk is using service names that the service model does not contain. Two vocabularies for the same thing, and reporting built on either excludes the other.
rules.source_tables_fields: incident business_service references, CSDM service records
rules.detection_logic: Incident service references with no matching CSDM service record, including free-text service values
rules.threshold_parameter: Includes free-text and legacy service fields where present
rules.evidence_to_show: The service values used in incidents, their volume, and the CSDM service list for comparison.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legacy service references retained on historical records.
rules.cross_domain_link: Two service vocabularies; blocks service-level reporting

rules.rule: SLA attached to a service with no offering (commitment structurally unenforceable)
rules.what_it_means: An SLA is attached to a service that has no Service Offering, so the commitment has no structure to attach to.
rules.why_it_matters: The SLA measures something the service model cannot express. Commitment reporting is structurally unenforceable, and any contractual target behind it has no measurable basis.
rules.source_tables_fields: SLA definitions and their service scope, CSDM service offering linkage
rules.detection_logic: SLA definitions scoped to services with zero offerings
rules.evidence_to_show: SLA definition, the service, its offering count, the incident volume under that SLA, and the commitment it is intended to enforce.
rules.false_positive_guard: Estate not using the offering layer.
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CSDM structural findings; commercial consequence

rules.rule: Change conflict detection producing no results because relationships are missing
rules.what_it_means: Change conflict detection is configured and produces no results, because the relationships it traverses do not exist.
rules.why_it_matters: The control runs, returns clean, and is structurally incapable of finding anything. This is the strongest single line available for a CAB audience, because the control they trust has never once worked.
rules.source_tables_fields: Conflict detection configuration and results, CI relationship depth for changed CIs
rules.detection_logic: Conflict detection configured with near-zero detections, where overlapping changes on related CIs existed and the relationships are absent
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires evidence that conflicts existed to be found
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — requires demonstrating both that the control ran and that detectable conflicts existed.
rules.evidence_to_show: Conflict detection configuration, detection count, the overlapping changes that existed, the CI relationship state between them, and the incidents that followed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely no conflicts in the window. Demonstrate the overlapping changes before asserting.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 for relationships, then the control begins working
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-058 and ITSM-084; the CAB-facing headline

rules.rule: Knowledge articles referenced in resolutions that are retired or unpublished
rules.what_it_means: Knowledge articles referenced in incident resolutions are retired or unpublished.
rules.why_it_matters: Agents are following guidance that was withdrawn. Either the article should not have been retired or the resolutions are citing stale material.
rules.source_tables_fields: Incident-to-article linkage, kb_knowledge state
rules.detection_logic: Incident resolutions referencing articles in a retired or unpublished state
rules.evidence_to_show: Article, its state and retirement date, the incidents referencing it since, and the replacement article if one exists.
rules.false_positive_guard: Article retired after the resolutions were written.
